title: Exploration diamond drilling
wikitext:
{{Short description|Technique of geological core drilling}} [[Image:Layne Rig57.jpg|thumb|Drilling rig capable of both diamond and reverse circulation drilling.]] '''Exploration diamond drilling''' is used in the mining industry to probe the contents of known [[ore]] deposits and potential sites. By withdrawing a small diameter core of rock from the orebody, [[geologists]] can analyze the core by [[Metallurgical assay|chemical assay]] and conduct [[petrology|petrologic]], [[structural]], and [[mineralogy|mineralogical]] studies of the rock. It is also often used in the [[geotechnical engineering]] industry for foundation testing in conjunction with soil sampling methods. The technique is named for the [[diamond]] encrusted [[drill bit]] used.{{cite book |last1=Hartman |first1=Howard L. |last2=Mutmansky |first2=Jan M. |title=Introductory Mining Engineering |date=9 August 2002 |publisher=John Wiley & Sons |isbn=978-0-471-34851-1 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Introductory_Mining_Engineering/jPdF6K0at4YC?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=Exploration+diamond+drilling&pg=PA68&printsec=frontcover |language=en}} ==History== [[File:Atlas Copco core bits.jpg|thumb|right|Diamond core drill bits]] Rodolphe Leschot is often cited as being the inventor of the first core bit in 1863.{{Cite web|url=https://www.petroleumhistory.org/OilHistory/pages/Diamond/inventor.html|title = Inventor and History}} Early [[diamond]] drilling opened up many new areas for mineral mining, and was related to a boom in mineral exploration in remote locations. Before the invention of the portable diamond drill, most mineral prospecting was limited to finding outcrops at the surface and hand digging. In the late 1970s, General Electric pioneered the technology of polycrystalline diamond compacts (PDCs) as a replacement for natural diamonds in drill bits.{{Citation |last1=Zhan |first1=Guodong (David) |chapter=Applications of Polycrystalline Diamond (PCD) Materials in Oil and Gas Industry |date=2022-10-06 |title=Applications and Use of Diamond |chapter-url=https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/83995 |access-date=2024-02-10 |publisher=IntechOpen |language=en |isbn=978-1-80356-318-3 |last2=Xu |first2=Jianhui |last3=He |first3=Duanwei}} ==Diamond drilling== [[Image:Edrockcore.jpg|thumb|upright|Illustration showing drill core]] Exploration diamond drilling differs from other geological drilling (such as [[Reverse circulation drilling|Reverse Circulation (RC) Drilling]]{{Cite web |title=Reverse Circulation (RC) drilling |url=https://www.devico.com/service/rc-drilling/ |access-date=2024-02-10 |website=Devico |language=en-GB}}) in that a solid core is extracted from depth, for examination on the surface. The key technology of the diamond drill is the actual diamond bit itself.{{Cite book |last=Marjoribanks |first=Roger |title=Geological Methods in Mineral Exploration and Mining |publisher=Springer Berlin Heidelberg |year=2010 |edition=2nd |pages=99–136}} It is composed of industrial diamonds set into a soft metallic matrix. As shown in the figure, the diamonds are scattered throughout the matrix, and the action relies on the matrix to slowly wear during the drilling process, so as to expose more diamonds. The bit is mounted onto a core barrel, that is attached to the [[drill string]], which is connected to a rotary drill rig. Drilling mud is injected into the drill pipe, so as to wash out the rock cuttings produced by the bit and also to reduce the heat produced due to friction which causes less wear and tear of the bits.{{Cite web |last=Team |first=B. O. P. |date=2022-11-04 |title=What is Drilling Mud and Why is it Important? |url=https://www.bop-products.com/blog/drilling/what-is-drilling-mud-and-why-is-it-important/ |access-date=2024-02-10 |website=BOP Products |language=en-US}} An actual diamond bit is a complex affair, usually designed for a specific rock type, with many channels for washing.{{cite book | last = de la Vergne | first = Jack | title = [[Hard Rock Miner's Handbook]] | publisher = McIntosh Engineering | date = 2003 | location = [[Tempe, Arizona|Tempe]]/[[North Bay, Ontario|North Bay]] | pages = 4–12 | isbn =0-9687006-1-6 }} The drill uses a [[diamond]] encrusted [[drill bit]] (pictured on the right) to drill through the rock. The drill produces a "core" which is photographed and split longitudinally. Half of the split core is [[Metallurgical assay|assayed]], while the other half is permanently stored for future use and re-assaying if necessary. Although a larger diameter core is the most preferred it is the most expensive. The most common wire line tube diameters and purposes are NQ (47.6mm) and HQ (63.5mm).{{cite web |url=https://app.boartlongyear.com/brochures/BitFieldGuide_Drilling%20Reference_april_2014_web_ready.pdf |title=Diamond Core Drilling Refeference: Dimensions, Weights and Volumes |website=app.boartlongyear.com |access-date=15 January 2023 }} ==Core extraction== [[Image:Usgsdrillcore.jpg|thumb|Extraction of core using triple-tube]] Merely advancing the drill by rotary action (and washing) causes a core to be extracted inside the barrel as shown. However, at a depth of perhaps 300 m, there must be a way to retrieve the core and take it to the surface. Constantly withdrawing the entire heavy drill pipe is impractical, so wireline drilling methods were developed to pull up the core inside the barrel.{{Cite web |last=Thomas |first=G. P. |date=2012-07-20 |title=Diamond Core Drilling: Theory, Mechanisms and Applications |url=https://www.azomining.com/Article.aspx?ArticleID=55 |access-date=2024-02-10 |website=AZoMining |language=en}} If the rock would always be solid granite, and the core would always break at the drill bit, then it would be a simple matter to stop the drilling, and lower a simple grabbing device by a wire and pull up the core. Unfortunately, many applications require an undisturbed core in fractured rock, which calls for elaborate wire-line devices.{{citation needed|date=July 2025}} The photo shows the extraction of a core, using a triple-tube wire-line system, capable of extracting core under the worst conditions.{{cite web|access-date=2015-08-13| url = http://users.metu.edu.tr/kok/pete424/PETE424_CHAPTER5.pdf| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160304230236/http://users.metu.edu.tr/kok/pete424/PETE424_CHAPTER5.pdf| url-status = dead| archive-date = 2016-03-04|title = Wire line coring}} This is very important when exploring fault zones such as the [[San Andreas Fault]]. ==Tube sizes== There are five major "wire line" tube sizes typically used. Larger tubes produce larger diameter rock cores and require more drill power to drive them. The choice of tube size is a trade-off between the rock core diameter desired and the depth that can be drilled with a particular [[drilling rig]] motor. extract: Exploration diamond drilling is used in the mining industry to probe the contents of known ore deposits and potential sites.  By withdrawing a small diameter core of rock from the orebody, geologists can analyze the core by chemical assay and conduct petrologic, structural, and mineralogical studies of the rock. It is also often used in the geotechnical engineering industry for foundation testing in conjunction with soil sampling methods. The technique is named for the diamond encrusted drill bit used.
